content: Papular purpuric gloves and socks syndrome (PPGSS) is a rare dermatological condition characterized by a distinct purpuric rash that is confined to the hands and feet. The condition has been associated with parvovirus B19 infection. Additionally, it has been linked to other viral infections, including human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6), measles, and coxsackievirus B6. PPGSS primarily affects teenagers and young adults. The clinical course of the disease is short, with symptoms such as rash and fever resolving completely within three days. The prognosis is benign, and complications are not typically observed. The syndrome is marked by symptoms such as pruritus (itching) and fever. On physical examination, findings include edema (swelling) and erythema (redness) of the hands and feet. Laboratory tests are generally normal, except for specific findings related to parvovirus B19. Serological testing reveals positive IgM antibodies for parvovirus B19, while IgG antibodies remain negative. Viral DNA testing can also confirm the presence of the virus.
